instructions: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Fill a big bowl with ice water and set it next to the stove.
Meanwhile, trim the stem ends off the green beans and mince the shallot.
In a large bowl, whisk the shallot with the 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, 2 tsp Dijon and a few grinds of pepper.
Add the beans to the boiling water and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until they're bright green and still have a little snap. Bite one to check.
Drain the beans and transfer them straight into the ice water for 2 minutes. Drain them well and pat them dry.
Add the beans to the bowl and toss until every bean is coated. Taste one. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.

Serve cold or at room temperature. For a packed lunch, keep the dressing in a jar and toss it with the beans just before eating, since the vinegar turns the beans a dull green if they sit in it for hours. Undressed beans keep 3 days in the fridge.
method_notes: Cup of Yum (the lead) blanches haricots verts for 4 to 5 minutes, chills them in ice water and tosses them with shallot, red wine vinegar, Dijon and olive oil, with an optional warm sauté. A Chef's Kitchen adds lemon, garlic, honey and walnuts, and the Dana's Table version steams and dresses them while warm; both were left out here to keep the plain mustard vinaigrette the dish is named for. Regular green beans work in place of the thin French ones and need a minute or two longer.
